1	# Project rules

3	These rules apply to every session on this repo. Follow them without being reminded.

5	## Git commits require explicit approval
6	
7	Never run `git commit` on your own initiative. Always ask first and wait for explicit confirmation before committing — even when wrapping up a session or completing a doc sweep.

12	
13	- **[`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) is the cross-subproject overview** — read it first if a task spans subprojects or if you're new to the repo. It points at each subproject's spec and journal.
14	- For non-trivial work inside a single subproject, read that subproject's spec **and** journal first (see below).
15	
16	## Journals are the source of truth for planning and progress
17	
18	This repo uses working journals to track planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress *outside* the chat context so they survive across sessions, compactions, and restarts.

24	- `firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md` — fretboard firmware (PIC32CM phototransistor **detector** node: ADC stream out; re-scoping from sensor/actuator — the actuator role is moving to the `guitar` subproject, but fretboard still actuates until that node is proven)

27	  - Spec for guitar lives at `firmware/guitar/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial guitar task.
28	- `tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md` — edge-ai (distill marvin's gameplay commands into a small ML model for the fretboard MCU)
29	  - Specs for edge-ai live under `tools/edge-ai/docs/` (`SPEC.md` + the doc map there) — read them alongside the journal on any non-trivial edge-ai task.
30	- `firmware/fauxmote/docs/journal.md` — fauxmote (ESP32 firmware emulating a Wiimote + guitar extension to a real Wii; parallel proof-of-concept)
31	  - Spec for fauxmote lives at `firmware/fauxmote/SPEC.md` — read it alongside the journal on any non-trivial fauxmote task.

35	When working on a subproject that has a journal:
36	
37	1. **Read the journal first.** Before responding to any non-trivial request, read the journal for that subproject. It contains the current focus, phased plan, open questions, decision log, and session log — the state you need to be useful.
38	2. **Update the journal as you go.** When we make a decision, resolve an open question, finish a plan phase, or finish a session, reflect that in the journal. Newest entries at the top within each section.
39	   - Decisions → append to the decision log with date and rationale.
40	   - Resolved open questions → remove from "Open questions" and add to the decision log with the answer and rationale.
41	   - Plan progress → check off phase items; add sub-bullets for anything learned during implementation.
42	   - Session close → add a dated session-log entry summarizing what happened.
43	3. **Prefer updating the journal over restating plans in chat.** If I'd otherwise write a multi-paragraph plan in chat, it belongs in the journal — the chat is ephemeral, the journal isn't.
44	4. **If a new subproject needs a journal, create one** using the same structure as `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`, and add it to the list above in this file.
45	
46	## Code comments describe current code only
47	
48	Comments in source files explain **what the code currently does and why**, when that's non-obvious. They are not a development diary.
49	
50	Do not put any of the following in source comments — they belong in the journal, commit messages, or PR descriptions:
51	
52	- Narrative of how the code evolved ("previously we did X, now we do Y", "this replaces the old …")
53	- Debug notes, troubleshooting history, or why something *doesn't* work
54	- TODO lists for future features (use the journal or an issue tracker)
55	- References to tasks, tickets, or past conversations ("fix for Greg's bug", "see chat from 2026-05-01")
56	- Extensive block comments explaining design rationale — a one-line "why" is fine; multi-paragraph prose goes in the journal
57	
58	**Default to no comment.** Only add one when removing it would confuse a future reader. If you catch yourself wanting to write a paragraph, write it in the journal instead and link from the code if needed (e.g. `// see firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md`).
